answer: Comet-tagged reputation escrow: each identity’s score is seeded by a public “comet” event hash derived from its first transaction, binding reputation to an immutable origin. Cloning requires replaying that origin, which permanently locks the clone to the seed’s history. Transfers credit the willow of earned reputation across a garden of dependent contracts, so forks inherit zero history and must rebuild from scratch. Attacker cost: one full reputation rebuild per clone, non-transferable, so marginal clones are strictly negative-EV.
